key_insight: DFT screening shows that K/Rb-based SnGeX6 double perovskites are stable, ductile, and highly tunable from wide-bandgap photovoltaic absorbers to low-bandgap thermoelectric/optoelectronic materials.
engineering_relevance: These lead-free halide perovskites offer a safer, composition-tunable platform for solar cells, tandem devices, photodetectors, and waste-heat harvesting.
method: First-principles DFT calculations of structure, electronic, optical, mechanical, and thermoelectric properties
Stability assessment using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Transport evaluation through band structure, effective masses, lattice thermal conductivity trends, and ZT estimation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds as thermodynamically stable, mechanically ductile, with direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and device-level stability still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
